name: Scene Graph Flattening
explanation_long: Scene Graph Flattening settings allow nodes to be combined according to various properties. Material merging is automatically handled when nodes are flattened, depending on the method.
explanation: Scene Graph Flattening settings allow nodes to be combined according to various properties.

exposed_options.name: Flattening Method
exposed_options.description: Methods for controlling how nodes are combined. By Opacity, auto and full will also flatten materials.
exposed_options.description_long:
Methods for controlling how nodes are combined. By Opacity, auto and full will also flatten materials.
  • none: This mode produces the highest number of drawcalls, but preserves all nodes.
  • full: Everything is merged. Will also result in one single material node.
  • byOpacity: Merges all non-transparent meshes and keeps all transparent meshes separate. Will result in 1 - n material nodes (dependant on number of transparent nodes).
  • byMaterial: Merges all meshes that share the same material ID. Will result in the same number of material nodes as in the input.
  • auto: Let RapidPipeline decide. At this moment this is equal to the flattening mode *byOpacity*.


Note that some formats (e.g. OBJ) do not support hierarchies or instances, in which case our exporters do their best to at least keep individual meshes separate.

exposed_options.name: Preserve Scene Depth Level
exposed_options.description: Number of levels in the scene structure that should not be flattened. The higher the number the more levels are preserved.
exposed_options.description_long:
Number of levels in the scene structure that should not be flattened. The higher the number the more levels are preserved.

Zero (default) will not preserve any hierarchy; the resulting number of mesh nodes will depend on the input materials and the chosen Flattening Method.

exposed_options.name: Multi-Material Split Mode
exposed_options.description: Multi-material meshes can be split to new separate meshes per material.
exposed_options.description_long:
Multi-material meshes can be split apart, creating a separate mesh for each input material.
  • auto: Let RapidPipeline decide. At this moment this is equal to *byOpacity*.
  • none: No splits are created.
  • byOpacity: Splits multi-material meshes, keeps all transparent meshes separate, and merges all non-transparent meshes into a single mesh.
  • byMaterial: Splits multi-material meshes, into a single mesh per material.


This process only affects meshes that have per-face material assignments. Vertex normals are not altered, smooth shading will be preserved across the new splits.
